defs.def: to fill or use a space, an area or an amount of time 使用，占用（空间、面积、时间等）

ex.s: It encourages us to occupy our own little corner, to avoid foolish leaps into the dark, to be satisfied.
ex.t: 而大众追求安稳和平庸。

ex.s: With their chins on their hands, they occupy themselves by staring out of the window or up at the ceiling.
ex.t: 他们手托下巴，要么望着窗外，要么盯着天花板，以此打发时间。

defs.def: to live or work in a room, house or building 使用（房屋、建筑）；居住

ex.s: But when Buck finished his ration and returned, he found his nest occupied.
ex.t: 但当巴克吃完他的口粮回来时，发现他的窝被占了。

defs.def: to enter a place in a large group and take control of it, especially by military force 侵占；占领；占据

ex.s: But on reflection, I can see how much of my time had been occupied with checking my phone.
ex.t: 但反思一下，我就能看出我多少时间都被查看手机占据了。

ex.s: In 1944, Saint-Exupéry left on a wartime mission over occupied France, from which he never returned.
ex.t: 1944年，圣埃克苏佩里出发执行一次飞越被占领法国上空的战时任务，从此再也没有回来。

ex.s: In 1937, the aggression of the Japanese army brought disaster to China’s three great universities: Peking University and Tsinghua University were occupied by Japanese troops, while Nankai University was completely destroyed by bombing.
ex.t: 1937年，日本军队的侵略给中国的三所著名大学带来了灾难：北京大学和清华大学被日军占领，而南开大学则被轰炸彻底摧毁。

defs.def: to fill your time or keep you busy doing sth 使忙于（做某事）；忙着（做某事）
to have an official job or position 任职；执政
